provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Numbers to 1000
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to count numbers up to 1000.
The pupils should be able to order numbers correctly.

Introduction:
We have learned to count numbers up to 500. Today we will learn to count up to 1000.

Content:
Counting numbers means saying numbers in order. We can count from 1 to 1000. We can use number lines to help us. Ordering numbers means arranging them from smallest to largest or largest to smallest. For example 100 200 300 is in order. 500 400 300 is reverse order.

Class activity:
Pupils will count numbers in class using a number line. They will also arrange number cards in order.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 1 to 100.
What comes after 499?
Arrange these numbers in order: 350 250 450 150.

Summary:
We can count and order numbers up to 1000.

topics.title: Place value to 1000
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to expand three digit numbers.
The pupils should be able to write number names.

Introduction:
We have learned about numbers up to 1000. Today we will learn about place value.

Content:
Place value means the value of a digit based on its position. In 365 the 3 is in the hundreds place. 3 hundreds is 300. The 6 is in the tens place. 6 tens is 60. The 5 is in the ones place. 5 ones is 5. We can write this as 300 + 60 + 5. Number names are how we say numbers in words. 365 is three hundred and sixty five.

Class activity:
Pupils will use number cards to show place value. They will also practice writing number names.

Evaluation questions:
Expand 426.
Write 278 in words.
What is the value of 9 in 945?

Summary:
Place value helps us understand numbers better.

topics.title: Addition of money
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to add prices.
The pupils should be able to solve shopping list problems.

Introduction:
We have learned to add numbers. Today we will learn to add money.

Content:
Money is used to buy things. In Nigeria we use naira and kobo. To add money we add the naira and kobo separately. For example if a book costs ₦120 and a pen costs ₦45 we add 120 + 45 = ₦165. When we go to the market we buy many things. We can add all the prices to find the total cost.

Class activity:
Pupils will play market game. They will add prices of items they buy.

Evaluation questions:
Add ₦35 and ₦27.
A book costs ₦120. A ruler costs ₦15. What is the total cost?
If you have ₦100 and buy an eraser for ₦20 how much money is left?

Summary:
We can add money to find total costs.

topics.title: Subtraction of money
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to calculate change from a purchase.
The pupils should be able to solve word problems.

Introduction:
We have learned to add money. Today we will learn to subtract money.

Content:
Subtraction means taking away. When we buy things we may need to find change. For example if you have ₦100 and buy a book for ₦75 we subtract 100-75 = ₦25. The ₦25 is your change. Word problems help us use subtraction in real life. For example if Mama bought rice for ₦350 and beans for ₦200 how much more did the rice cost?

Class activity:
Pupils will role play buying things in a market. They will calculate change.

Evaluation questions:
Subtract ₦48 from ₦100.
You have ₦200. You buy a shoe for ₦125. How much change do you get?
A bag costs ₦150. A cap costs ₦80. How much more does the bag cost?

Summary:
We can subtract money to find change.

topics.title: Multiplication by 6 to 10
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall multiplication tables.
The pupils should be able to solve word problems.

Introduction:
We have learned multiplication tables up to 5. Today we will learn tables up to 10.

Content:
Multiplication is repeated addition. For example 3 × 4 means 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. We can use tables to help us multiply. The table of 6 is 6 12 18 24 30 36 42 48 54 60. Word problems help us use multiplication in real life. For example if one egg costs ₦10 how much do 7 eggs cost? We multiply 7 × 10 = ₦70.

Class activity:
Pupils will practice multiplication tables using songs and games.

Evaluation questions:
What is 8 × 7?
If one book costs ₦15 how much do 4 books cost?
Complete the table: 9 × 3 = ?

Summary:
Multiplication helps us find total costs quickly.

topics.title: Division with remainders
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to share items and find remainders.
The pupils should be able to solve real life sharing problems.

Introduction:
We have learned division without remainders. Today we will learn division with remainders.

Content:
Division is sharing things equally. Sometimes we have leftovers. For example if we have 10 mangoes to share among 3 children each child gets 3 mangoes. We have 1 mango left. This is the remainder. We write it as 10 ÷ 3 = 3 remainder 1. In real life we share things like money, food or toys. Sometimes there is always something left over.

Class activity:
Pupils will share counters among groups and find remainders.

Evaluation questions:
Share 15 oranges among 4 children. How many each? What is the remainder?
If you have ₦27 to share among 5 friends how much each? What is left?
Divide 20 by 6. What is the remainder?

Summary:
Division can have remainders when things cannot be shared equally.

topics.title: Capacity and time
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to measure capacity in litres.
The pupils should be able to tell time in minutes.

Introduction:
We have learned about length and weight. Today we will learn about capacity and time.

Content:
Capacity is how much a container can hold. We measure capacity in litres. A small bottle may hold 1 litre. A big drum may hold 200 litres. We can compare containers by their capacity. Time is measured in minutes and hours. There are 60 minutes in one hour. We use time to plan our day. School starts at 8 am and ends at 2 pm.

Class activity:
Pupils will measure water using litre jugs. They will also practice telling time.

Evaluation questions:
Which holds more a 1 litre bottle or a 5 litre bucket?
How many minutes in one hour?
School starts at 8 am. How many minutes until 10 am?

Summary:
Capacity and time help us measure and plan.

topics.title: Data handling
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to use tally marks and pictographs.
The pupils should be able to read and interpret charts.

Introduction:
We have learned to collect information. Today we will learn to show information.

Content:
Data is information we collect. We can show data using tally marks. Each tally mark is one item. Four tallies make a group of five. We can use pictographs to show data. A pictograph uses pictures to show numbers. For example one picture of a mango may mean 5 mangoes. We can read charts to find information quickly.

Class activity:
Pupils will collect data on favorite fruits and make a pictograph.

Evaluation questions:
Draw 7 tally marks.
One picture means 2 pupils. How many pupils for 3 pictures?
What is the most popular fruit in your class pictograph?

Summary:
We can show data using tally marks and pictographs.

topics.title: Everyday arithmetic
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to combine addition and subtraction.
The pupils should be able to solve multi step problems.

Introduction:
We have learned different operations. Today we will learn to use them together.

Content:
Sometimes we need to use more than one operation to solve problems. For example if you have ₦100 buy a book for ₦35 and a pen for ₦20 you first add 35 + 20 = ₦55 then subtract 100-55 = ₦45. Multi step problems have more than one part. We solve them step by step. For example if a danfo has 30 passengers and 12 get off then 8 get on how many passengers are there now? First 30-12 = 18 then 18 + 8 = 26.

Class activity:
Pupils will solve multi step word problems in groups.

Evaluation questions:
Add 45 and 27 then subtract 30.
You have ₦200. Buy a shirt for ₦85 and shorts for ₦60. How much left?
A bus has 40 passengers. 15 get off at first stop. 10 get on at second stop. How many now?

Summary:
We can combine operations to solve problems.

topics.title: Revision and assessment
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The pupils should be able to recall all topics covered.
The pupils should be able to solve problems accurately.

Introduction:
We have learned many topics this term. Today we will revise and be assessed.

Content:
We will review all topics we covered this term. This includes numbers to 1000 place value addition subtraction multiplication division capacity time and data handling. We will practice solving different types of problems. Assessment helps us know what we have learned well and what we need to improve.

Class activity:
Pupils will participate in a problem solving fair with different stations.

Evaluation questions:
Count from 900 to 1000.
Add ₦75 and ₦48.
What is 9 × 8?
Share 20 pencils among 5 children.
How many minutes in half an hour?

Summary:
We have learned many important math skills this term.
